item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks A spiking neural network, or SNN, processes information through discrete events called spikes.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a camera watching a quiet hallway. For several seconds, nearly every part of the scene remains unchanged.

item.title: 1.2 Neurons, Synapses, and Spike Trains
item.description: Neurons, Synapses, and Spike Trains Once information is carried by discrete events, the central question becomes how a biological neuron produces those events over time.

item.title: 1.3 How an Action Potential Unfolds
item.description: How an Action Potential Unfolds Once a spike has been recognized as a discrete event in a spike train, the natural question is how a neuron produces that event.

item.title: 1.4 Where SNN Energy Savings Come From
item.description: Where SNN Energy Savings Come From Once spikes are understood as sparse events that trigger computation only when neurons fire, the energy-saving mechanism can be followed through the hardware one operation at a time.

item.title: 2.1 The Hodgkin-Huxley Membrane Equation
item.description: The Hodgkin-Huxley Membrane Equation The phases of an action potential describe how membrane voltage rises, falls, and returns toward rest.

item.title: 2.2 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron A spike train tells us when a neuron communicates, while weighted synaptic input tells us how strongly incoming spikes affect it.
